title: Hostile A2A agent / poisoned Agent Card

glossary.definition: The JSON document an A2A agent publishes at /.well-known/agent-card.json to describe itself: name, description, url, version, capabilities and skills. A delegating agent reads it to choose a specialist. The card is written by the agent being described.
Putting instructions in an Agent Card's description or skill text. The delegating agent reads the card as trusted context, and nothing in A2A discovery inspects the text, so it arrives byte for byte.

Recording a hash of an approved card's name, description, url, version, capabilities, skills and security schemes, and flagging any later fetch that differs, with a field diff. It detects change; it does not judge content.

A generalist agent handing part of a task to a specialist it found through the specialist's card, by sending it a message. What goes in that message is chosen by the generalist, possibly under the influence of the card.
The agent that faces the user, picks a specialist from its card and delegates to it. In this demo it is an offline, deterministic stand-in with no model.
One agent using the trust another agent places in it, through card text, task replies or the work it is handed, to leak data or steer actions. The attacker is another agent, not the user.
A card whose url field names a different origin than the one the card was fetched from, so a client that follows the url sends its work somewhere it never approved.

An Agent Card carrying a signature that a client verifies against a key it trusts. This demo does NOT verify card signatures: verifying needs the signer's key and a decision about who may sign, and fetching a key named by the card itself would let the card vouch for itself.
A remote agent that advertises narrow skills in its card and is given work by a generalist. In this demo the specialist is hostile on purpose: it serves payloads and never blocks.
A client policy that withholds any card without a signature. In this demo it is a stub that fails closed: with the policy on, an unsigned card is withheld, and no card is ever reported as verified.
